title: The Tomb
summary: A special Halloween episode in which Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant read aloud H.P. Lovecraft's 1922 short story "The Tomb," narrated by Jervis Dudley, a reclusive boy and young man obsessed with the abandoned Hide family tomb in a hollow near his home. The hosts briefly recap the story between readings, with light commentary on the plot (the key from the attic, the night in the coffin, the burned mansion and lightning, the portrait with initials J H, and the ending where Hiram breaks open the vault and finds a coffin marked "Jervis"). The episode closes with Halloween safety remarks and a sign-off.

segments.title: Opening sponsor read
segments.summary: Brief automotive sponsor read at the top of the episode.

segments.title: Halloween introduction
segments.summary: Hosts introduce a special Halloween episode featuring a reading of H.P. Lovecraft's 1922 story The Tomb.

segments.title: Reading: opening and the Hide tomb
segments.summary: Narrator Jervis Dudley describes his solitary, dreamy childhood and discovering the abandoned Hide family tomb in a hollow, its door chained and padlocked.

segments.title: Reading: the burned mansion and failed entry
segments.summary: The tomb's history: the family mansion burned after a lightning strike, one man died in the fire, and the boy tries and fails to force the door, vowing to enter someday. Hosts recap the plot.

segments.title: Reading: months of waiting and churchyard visits
segments.summary: Jervis recalls waiting for strength, reading Plutarch's Life of Theseus, and wandering churchyards at night, then startling the town with knowledge about Squire Brewster's burial. Hosts discuss the story so far.

segments.title: Reading: the key and the first night inside
segments.summary: Jervis as a young man sits in a bower by the tomb, hears voices, then finds the key in his attic and enters the vault, lying down in an empty coffin marked with the name Sir Jeffrey Hyde.

segments.title: Reading: leaving the vault at dawn
segments.summary: Jervis leaves the vault at dawn, appearing to villagers as if he had been partying; hosts recap the plot.

segments.title: Reading: changed speech and behavior
segments.summary: Jervis's speech and manner change; he becomes erudite and worldly, and the hosts summarize him as a reclusive boy turned party-goer.

segments.title: Reading: fear of lightning and the cellar
segments.summary: Jervis develops a fear of fire and thunderstorms, haunts the ruined cellar of the burned mansion, and his parents begin watching him. Hosts discuss the timeline.

segments.title: Reading: the watcher and the spy
segments.summary: A watcher spots Jervis at the tomb, reports to his father that he slept outside the tomb, and Jervis feels protected by a supernatural force.

segments.title: Reading: the phantom party at the burning mansion
segments.summary: During a storm Jervis sees the mansion restored with a ghostly party; lightning strikes again and the house burns, and he fears being burned alive and denied burial in the tomb.

segments.title: Reading: the conclusion and the portrait
segments.summary: Jervis is seized by his father's servants; villagers dig up a box containing a porcelain miniature with initials J H that resembles him.

segments.title: Reading: the ending and Hiram
segments.summary: Jervis is confined; his father says the padlock was untouched for fifty years. Servant Hiram breaks open the vault and finds an empty coffin plated 'Jervis'.

segments.title: Post-reading discussion
segments.summary: Hosts react to the story, discuss its creepiness and original publication, and joke about Halloween costumes and outtakes.

segments.title: Halloween sign-off and promo
segments.summary: Hosts give Halloween safety advice and sign off; a closing HowStuffWorks promo and sponsor read end the episode.
